name: Configuration Change History and Drift Record
description: The record of how a security-relevant configuration changed over the examination period, and of any deviation from an approved baseline, together with how deviations were detected and resolved. This is the companion artifact that converts point-in-time configuration evidence into period coverage for a Type 2 conclusion.

expected_content.element: Chronological record of changes to the in-scope configuration across the full examination period
expected_content.why: This is the entire purpose of the artifact: to show what the configuration was, not just what it is now.

expected_content.element: Actor and timestamp for each change
expected_content.why: Attribution converts a change log into evidence that changes were authorised.

expected_content.element: Before and after values, or a reference to the versioned definition
expected_content.why: A record that something changed without saying to what cannot evidence that the control held.

expected_content.element: Deviations from the approved baseline, with detection time and resolution time
expected_content.why: Drift detection is the operating substance of the control; without it, the baseline is aspirational.

expected_content.element: Statement of the period the extract covers and confirmation it is unfiltered
expected_content.why: A change log covering part of the period silently understates drift.

expected_content.element: Link to the approval or change record for each change
expected_content.why: Connects this artifact to the change management control where one applies.

source_system_examples: Cloud security posture management drift alerts

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default: the extract must reach the end of the period under assessment. The 30-day window applies to continuous monitoring outside a formal period.

redaction_guidance: Change logs frequently embed secrets in before/after values. Redact credential material rather than supplying raw diffs.
Retain actor identity; anonymising it destroys the attribution the artifact exists to provide.
retention_guidance: Retain for the examination period plus the following period, since this artifact is what makes earlier point-in-time evidence usable.

validation_rules.rule: A change history extract exists for each in-scope configuration surface.
The extract spans the full examination period with no gaps in coverage.
The extract is generated by the platform's own audit facility rather than compiled by hand.
Deviations from baseline show both detection time and resolution time, so drift duration can be assessed.
The extract reaches the end of the examination period.

common_issues.issue: Log retention is shorter than the examination period, so early months cannot be evidenced.
common_issues.impact: Point-in-time configuration evidence cannot be extended across the period, weakening every control that depends on this pairing.

common_issues.issue: Drift is detected but the resolution time is not recorded.
common_issues.impact: Detection can be shown; correction cannot, so the control's corrective element is unevidenced.

common_issues.issue: Extract covers one account or region while the boundary spans several.
common_issues.impact: Drift outside the extracted scope is invisible.

source_refs.supports: Expected content, persuasiveness weighting, and the common issues list.
Freshness window, sensitivity classification, and redaction guidance.

notes: Deliberately generalised across configuration surfaces rather than duplicated per control. It supports identity, encryption, and boundary controls alike, which is why applicable_controls is multi-valued.
Closes the type2_pairing_requirement gap recorded against EV-IAM-001 in the foundation phase.
